source.title: Multi-Dimensional Featurizers Yield Fine-Grained Steering and Data Shaping in Robot Foundation Models
source.authors: Aiden Swann; Mozes Jacobs; Mathilde Papillon; S. Boppana; David Chanin; Dron Hazra; Usha Bhalla; Curt Tigges; Mac Schwager; Owen Lewis; Jack Merullo; E. Lubana; Atticus Geiger; Thomas Fel; Matthew Kowal

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares learned block-sparse features with one-dimensional SAE features and measures feature geometry in robot foundation models. This is a conceptual test of whether the relevant representations can be multidimensional, not a reproduction of the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test sparse-feature competition, interference, or a sparsity-dependent superposition transition. Its relevant evidence is the measured geometry of learned BSF features and comparisons with SAE features. Steering and data-shaping outcomes are not rows here because they do not measure feature dimensionality itself.
record.test_reason: The study trains matched block-sparse featurizers (BSFs) and scalar SAEs on about 52M unpooled vision-language-action (VLA) activations. It reports within-block stable rank and feature geometry, which bear on whether represented features are 1-D directions (V6). This is a new setting (robot foundation models) with a new method, not the toy-model setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that BSFs recover interpretable multi-dimensional features in VLA models, validated causally by steering. They also find that feature-guided masking of about 1.4% of tokens delays failure recovery while keeping task performance. They note that BSFs are not uniformly superior to SAEs and that how the features emerge remains unexplained.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains and compares block-sparse featurizers and SAE baselines on robot-model activations; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method or its feature-overlap experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that stable rank changes with block dimension and remains below block dimension; feature discovery and comparisons also vary by featurizer type (BSF versus SAE).

fits_no_version.finding: BSF features yield larger per-feature ablation effects on predicted end-effector position and higher single-feature task-variable decodability than matched SAEs across layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-dimensional featurizer units align better with causally relevant task variables than scalar SAE units in VLA models.

record.problems: The geometry examples are qualitative and selected; the paper does not establish ground-truth feature units or show that the observed blocks are complete or canonical. It does not test superposition capacity pressure, sparsity-dependent interference, or the original toy-model transition.
record.rows_left_out: Open- and closed-loop steering and data-shaping results are omitted because their outcomes measure behavioral interventions or policy performance, not the dimensionality of the represented features.

untested.parts: No toy networks, no sparsity sweep or phase transition, no interference or near-orthogonality geometry.
No test of capacity competition, feature importance or dedicated dimensions.
No analysis of neuron polysemanticity or its causes.
No LLMs. No neuron-level analysis of features spread across many neurons; SAE recovery is not assessed as evidence of superposition.
Completeness and stability across seeds of SAE features are not tested; only fragmentation in selected examples.

Not tested in LLMs or toy models. No test that these multi-dimensional features are themselves superposed (more features than dimensions). No random or 1-D-ground-truth control showing BSF stable rank exceeds what grouping several 1-D features would give.

missing.what: Per-layer BSF vs SAE comparison of single-feature ablation effect and decodability (ridge-probe R2) at matched coordinate budgets
Open-loop steering feature counts and held-out recovery for BSF, Fisher BSF and SAE at the semantic, visual and geometric sites, including cases where SAEs equal or beat BSFs
Reconstruction R2 and action log-likelihood change versus block size (SAE b=1 as special case)

record.verdict_notes: Changed tranche to T3 (new setting: robot VLA models). Row states were recast relative to V6's 1-D claim, since multi-dimensional structure counts against it. Qualitative rows that cannot separate grouped 1-D features from irreducible ones are marked cannot_determine. All geometry examples are author-selected. Stable rank is bounded by the imposed block size and has no control for merging 1-D features.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; no test of overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise through non-capacity mechanisms.
The systems studied are vision-language-action robot models, not LLMs tested for feature distribution across neurons or SAE recovery of sparse features.
The paper does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model's representation.
The paper measures learned multidimensional feature geometry in robot models, but does not establish that these features are the units of superposition in the original toy-model sense.

rows.subject: MolmoACT2
rows.operation_detail: Measured within-block stable rank for SAE and BSF features.
rows.note: The paper states that both Vanilla and Fisher BSFs grow in stable rank more slowly than block dimension.
rows.check: The state should be judged against V6. A mean stable rank of about 5.3 in 16-dim blocks is well above 1, i.e. multi-dimensional, opposite to V6. The baseline should be 1 (the 1-D prediction), with 16 as the ceiling. Caveat: the block size is imposed by the featurizer, so one block could merge several 1-D features.

rows.subject: MolmoACT2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the geometry of visual feature F2973 across timesteps.
rows.value: The block's activation geometry varies with the appearance of markers at different stages of manipulation.
rows.note: The paper presents this as a block capturing recognizable visual content together with variation within that content.
rows.check: A selected qualitative display of variation inside a 3-D block. It does not test whether that variation reduces to several 1-D features, and there is no SAE comparison for this feature.

rows.subject: MolmoACT2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the geometry of visual feature F2571 across robot parts.
rows.measure: Organization of activations by robot part
rows.value: The block organizes image patches from different parts of the arm into different regions.
rows.note: A qualitative example of variation within one BSF feature.
rows.check: Selected qualitative example. Different arm parts occupying regions of a block does not show the feature is irreducibly multi-dimensional.

rows.subject: π0.5
rows.operation_detail: Examined a visual-language container feature and compared its geometry with SAE assignments.
rows.measure: Organization of container-related vision and text activations
rows.baseline: Three SAE features tile much of the displayed text-token geometry
rows.value: One BSF feature represents related container groups in distinct spatial regions and activates across image and text tokens.
rows.note: The authors describe one block spanning related concepts that are divided among multiple SAE features.
rows.check: Against V6: one block holds structure that three SAE latents split up. Also bears on V5, since the SAE latents fragment one container feature. The SAE tiling is a comparator description, not a baseline value. The example is selected.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 6 caption; Section 3.3, Visual-Language Features, text lines 490–506

rows.subject: MolmoACT2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the geometry of a gripper-state feature and compared it with SAE assignments.
rows.measure: Organization of activations by gripper opening and gripper side
rows.baseline: Exactly one SAE feature tiles each side of the gripper
rows.value: The BSF forms an X-shaped point cloud organized by gripper opening and the side on which it activates.
rows.note: The paper describes the BSF as bringing complementary views of a changing two-sided gripper into one feature.
rows.check: X-shaped manifold organised by gripper opening, captured in one block while SAE latents tile each side. Selected qualitative example; the SAE tiling is a comparator, not a baseline.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.3, Task and Control Variables; Figure 7 caption, text lines 507–535

rows.subject: π0.5
rows.operation_detail: Examined a feature's geometry against end-effector coordinates during an episode.
rows.measure: Relationship between feature geometry and end-effector Cartesian coordinates
rows.value: The feature varies with end-effector x, y, and z position over an episode.
rows.note: The model receives joint angles rather than explicit Cartesian end-effector coordinates, according to the paper.
rows.check: Covariation with end-effector x, y, z could equally be three 1-D features grouped in one block. There is no test of irreducibility and no SAE comparison.

rows.subject: MolmoBot
rows.operation_detail: Related feature geometry to camera position relative to the robot.
rows.measure: Organization by camera side and camera position
rows.value: The feature captures camera viewpoint properties, including whether the camera is to the robot's left or right.
rows.note: The paper identifies this as a feature combining observation-viewpoint and robot-state information.
rows.check: Qualitative viewpoint organisation; the measure cannot separate a multi-dimensional feature from grouped 1-D ones. The subject is MolmoBot, a simulation-trained model.

rows.subject: MolmoACT2
rows.operation_detail: Examined a BSF feature's geometry against proprioceptive state values and component identity.
rows.measure: Organization of feature geometry by quantized state value and state-component index
rows.value: The feature forms three looping branches that converge into a common extension; state values are ordered along the curves, with further structure by component identity.
rows.note: The paper describes a manifold organizing both numeric value and component identity.
rows.check: Nonlinear looping manifold ordered by state value, i.e. not a single direction. Selected example; the feature id is not stated.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.3, Proprioceptive Features; Figure 8 caption, text lines 520–529 and 602–603

rows.subject: π0.5
rows.operation_detail: Examined the geometry of a failure-recovery feature and compared it with SAE assignments.
rows.measure: Geometry of activations during grasp failures and corrections
rows.baseline: Multiple SAE features tile the structure
rows.value: A three-dimensional BSF feature captures a distinctly nonlinear, conical structure associated with recovery from failed grasps.
rows.note: The feature was identified from the authors' rollout data and is shown activating during missed grasps and corrections.
rows.check: Conical nonlinear geometry that multiple SAE latents tile. The feature was found from the authors' own rollouts; selected example.

relationships.condition: VLA models (MolmoAct2, π0.5) analysed with BSFs
relationships.reason: Stable rank is about 5.3 in 16-dim blocks (r1), and selected features show nonlinear manifolds that SAEs split across several latents (r4, r5, r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Blocks had a stable rank of about 5.3 out of 16 dimensions, and selected features showed nonlinear manifolds that SAEs split across several latents.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: VLA models (MolmoAct2, π0.5) analysed with BSFs
source_check.reason: r1 reports effective rank above one; r4, r5, r8 and r9 describe structured geometries extending beyond a single direction. This challenges one-direction feature descriptions in the tested setting, while superposition between these units remains untested.

relationships.condition: Steering and per-layer comparisons on MolmoAct2 (from text; not in rows)
relationships.reason: Text, Fig. 4: one SAE latent matches one BSF block for geometric steering (98.2% vs 99.7%). SAEs transfer visual steering better (97.3% vs 84.6%), and authors say BSFs are not uniformly superior.
relationships.display_finding: One SAE latent matched one multi-dimensional BSF block for geometric steering (98.2% vs 99.7%), SAEs transferred visual steering better (97.3% vs 84.6%), and the authors say BSFs are not uniformly superior.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Steering and per-layer comparisons on MolmoAct2 (from text; not in rows)
source_check.reason: Figure 4 accurately reports comparable geometric steering and better SAE visual transfer, but those outcomes test intervention effectiveness rather than whether represented features are one-dimensional. Nonuniform BSF superiority is not a qualification of V6.

relationships.condition: Selected VLA features where SAE latents tile one BSF manifold
relationships.reason: SAE latents fragment single variables (container, gripper, recovery) into arcs or regions, so they are not canonical units there (r4, r5, r9). The evidence is qualitative and selected.
relationships.display_finding: SAE latents split variables such as container, gripper and recovery into arcs or regions, though the evidence is qualitative and from selected features.

source_check.condition: Selected VLA features where SAE latents tile one BSF manifold
source_check.reason: r4, r5 and r9 show selected interpretable variables divided among SAE latents while grouped within individual BSF blocks, qualifying an individual-latent interpretation of units. This supports only the stated qualitative scope limit, not a general finding about completeness, stability or ground-truth canonical units.

relation.reason: Its own stable-rank measurements and feature geometries bear on V6; selected SAE tiling comparisons also qualify interpretations of individual dictionary units.

tranche.reason: The study reports feature-dimensionality results in a new setting, vision-language-action robot models, using matched BSFs and scalar SAEs.

source_check.notes: The r1 comparator of 16 is a stated dimensional upper bound; the relevant one-direction reference for V6 is rank 1. Selected BSF manifolds do not establish ground-truth canonical units or superposition between those units.

statements.correction: Selected container, gripper and recovery geometries are partitioned among SAE latents and grouped within individual BSF blocks; comparisons are qualitative; cross-configuration stability and ground-truth canonical units are not established.
statements.problem: The robot examples and layer assignments are correct, but configuration-invariant individual units are not directly tested.

statements.correction: MolmoAct2 layer 13, k=32: mean stable rank approximately 5.3 at block dimension 16. Figure 4: geometric held-out recovery 99.7% for one BSF block and 98.2% for one SAE latent; visual held-out recovery 84.6% for Vanilla BSF and 97.3% for SAE. These steering comparisons measure intervention effectiveness and transfer.
statements.problem: The rank, geometries and steering comparisons are accurate, but steering performance does not establish a scope limit on V6's dimensionality claim.

statements.correction: The study measures recovered feature geometry and behavioral relevance; it does not measure superposition between recovered multidimensional units or compare represented feature count with model capacity.
statements.problem: The identified question is untested, but the study does not explicitly discuss leaving multidimensional superposition or a feature-capacity comparison open.

statements.correction: The robot study reports multidimensional feature geometry and causal interventions; superposition between those units is not tested. Its explicit limitations concern feature emergence, participation in policy computation and intervention generalization.
statements.problem: The evidential distinction is correct, but attributing an explicit statement about the superposition link to this robot study is unsupported.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Measured BSF feature geometry in the tested robot foundation models
reader_labels.reason: The reported stable rank and qualitative examples show multidimensional feature structure, including cases where one BSF block groups variation tiled across multiple SAE features (r1-r9).
